claim: African Americans carrying two APOL1 risk alleles have a high odds ratio for HIVAN (OR 29).
source: We hypothesized that PKR activation is a mechanistic pathway shared by HIV- and APOL1-mediated nephropathies, considering the high odds ratio for HIVAN among African Americans (OR 29) and South Africans (OR 89) carrying two APOL1 risk alleles (Kasembeli et al., 2015).

claim: South Africans carrying two APOL1 risk alleles have a high odds ratio for HIVAN (OR 89).

claim: The trans-activating regions RNA in the HIV-1 long terminal repeats at the 5' and 3' ends of the HIV genome form dsRNA structures.
source: The trans-activating regions RNA in the HIV-1 long terminal repeats at the 5' and 3' ends of the HIV genome form dsRNA structures and induce PKR autophosphorylation, thereby activating PKR (Carpick et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Carpick et al., 1997.

claim: The trans-activating regions RNA in the HIV-1 long terminal repeats induce PKR autophosphorylation, thereby activating PKR.

claim: PKR is a potent driver of many stress response pathways, including translational shutdown, apoptosis, inflammation, and metabolism.
source: As PKR is a potent driver of many stress response pathways, including translational shutdown, apoptosis, inflammation, and metabolism, we hypothesized that PKR inhibition by the PKR-specific oxoindole/imidazole inhibitor C16 might rescue kidney injury in Tg26 mice.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PKR's role in cellular stress responses.

claim: C16-treated Tg26 mice had lower serum creatinine compared to control Tg26 mice.
source: C16-treated Tg26 mice had lower serum creatinine (Figure 1A), reduced albuminuria (Figure 1B and C), and reduced pPKR abundance (Figure 1D–G) compared to control Tg26 mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: C16-treated Tg26 mice had reduced albuminuria compared to control Tg26 mice.
source: C16-treated Tg26 mice had lower serum creatinine (Figure 1A), reduced albuminuria (Figure 1B and C), and reduced pPKR abundance (Figure 1D–G) compared to control Tg26 mice.

claim: C16-treated Tg26 mice had reduced pPKR abundance compared to control Tg26 mice.
source: C16-treated Tg26 mice had lower serum creatinine (Figure 1A), reduced albuminuria (Figure 1B and C), and reduced pPKR abundance (Figure 1D–G) compared to control Tg26 mice.

claim: C16 treatment reduced urinary excretion of the kidney injury marker neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) in Tg26 mice.
source: Further, C16 treatment reduced urinary excretion of the kidney injury marker neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) (Figure 1H).

claim: At 12 weeks of age, there was less glomerulosclerosis in C16-treated Tg26 mice compared to untreated Tg26 mice.

claim: At 12 weeks of age, there was less microtubular dilatation in C16-treated Tg26 mice compared to untreated Tg26 mice.

claim: C16 treatment reduced fibrosis extent in Tg26 mice, quantified by Picrosirius Red staining.
source: Histomorphological quantification confirmed that C16 treatment reduced glomerular injury, assessed as segmental glomerulosclerosis and global glomerulosclerosis (Figure 1L and M), and as fibrosis extent, quantified by Picrosirius Red staining (Figure 1N–Q).

claim: Single-nucleus RNA-seq profiled 56,976 nuclei from kidney samples.
source: Single-nucleus RNA-seq profiled 56,976 nuclei.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the number of nuclei analyzed in the study.

claim: 23 cell clusters were identified in the single-nucleus RNA-seq analysis.
source: We identified 23-cell clusters, including a novel cell type (PT-Mito, proximal tubule cell cluster with a higher expression level of mitochondrial genes compared to adjacent cells), as shown as a uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) plot (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: A novel cell type (PT-Mito) was identified, which is a proximal tubule cell cluster with a higher expression level of mitochondrial genes compared to adjacent cells.
source: We identified 23-cell clusters, including a novel cell type (PT-Mito, proximal tubule cell cluster with a higher expression level of mitochondrial genes compared to adjacent cells), as shown as a uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) plot (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The gene encoding PKR, Eif2ak2, was expressed in glomeruli and all tubular segments.
source: The gene encoding PKR, Eif2ak2, was expressed in glomeruli and all tubular segments (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).

claim: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) results of bulk RNA-seq showed that mitochondrial-related pathways were the most downregulated pathway in Tg26 mice when compared with WT mice.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) results of bulk RNA-seq showed that mitochondrial-related pathways were the most downregulated pathway in Tg26 mice when compared with WT mice, suggesting that mitochondrial gene transcription (for both nuclear-genome and mitochondrial genome-encoded genes) was significantly downregulated (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Mitochondrial gene transcription (for both nuclear-genome and mitochondrial genome-encoded genes) was significantly downregulated in Tg26 mice compared to WT mice.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) results of bulk RNA-seq showed that mitochondrial-related pathways were the most downregulated pathway in Tg26 mice when compared with WT mice, suggesting that mitochondrial gene transcription (for both nuclear-genome and mitochondrial genome-encoded genes) was significantly downregulated (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is inferred from GSEA results shown in Figure 3A.

claim: C16 treatment reversed the downregulation of mitochondrial genes in Tg26 mice.
source: Expression levels of specific mitochondrial genes were assessed (Figure 3B) and showed that C16 treatment reversed the downregulation of these mitochondrial genes (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: Western blot analyses showed lower abundance of mitochondrial complex I and II in Tg26 kidney.
source: Western blot analyses were consistent with bulk RNA-seq results showing lower abundance of mitochondrial complex I and II in Tg26 kidney and this was restored to normal by C16 treatment (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: C16 treatment restored the abundance of mitochondrial complex I and II to normal in Tg26 kidney.
source: Western blot analyses were consistent with bulk RNA-seq results showing lower abundance of mitochondrial complex I and II in Tg26 kidney and this was restored to normal by C16 treatment (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: Mitochondrial DNA copy numbers were decreased in Tg26 mice.
source: Mitochondrial DNA copy numbers were decreased in Tg26 mice, but C16 treatment did not reverse these changes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: C16 treatment did not reverse the decrease in mitochondrial DNA copy numbers in Tg26 mice.
source: Mitochondrial DNA copy numbers were decreased in Tg26 mice, but C16 treatment did not reverse these changes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: PKR inhibition by C16 rescued transcriptional downregulation of both nuclear-encoded and mitochondrial-encoded mitochondrial genes.
source: These findings suggest that PKR inhibition by C16 rescued transcriptional downregulation of both nuclear-encoded and mitochondrial-encoded mitochondrial genes, but the rescue was not through increased mitochondrial DNA copy number.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data on gene expression and mitochondrial DNA copy numbers.

claim: The rescue of mitochondrial gene expression by C16 was not through increased mitochondrial DNA copy number.
source: These findings suggest that PKR inhibition by C16 rescued transcriptional downregulation of both nuclear-encoded and mitochondrial-encoded mitochondrial genes, but the rescue was not through increased mitochondrial DNA copy number.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that C16 rescued gene expression but did not increase mtDNA copy number.

claim: Single-nucleus RNA-seq and subsequent pathway analysis showed that the majority of cell types manifested global downregulation of mitochondrial-expressed genes in Tg26 kidneys.
source: Single-nucleus RNA-seq and subsequent pathway analysis showed that the majority of cell types, including mitochondrial proximal tubules (PT-Mito), PT-S1, injured PT (PT-Inj), and endothelial cells, manifested global downregulation of mitochondrial-expressed genes in Tg26 kidneys and that this decline was rescued by C16 treatment (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by pathway analysis data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The decline in mitochondrial-expressed genes in Tg26 kidneys was rescued by C16 treatment.
source: Single-nucleus RNA-seq and subsequent pathway analysis showed that the majority of cell types, including mitochondrial proximal tubules (PT-Mito), PT-S1, injured PT (PT-Inj), and endothelial cells, manifested global downregulation of mitochondrial-expressed genes in Tg26 kidneys and that this decline was rescued by C16 treatment (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by pathway analysis data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The PT-Mito cluster consisted of 3.1–5.8% of kidney cortex cells.
source: Based on unbiased clustering, we identified a distinct proximal tubule cell cluster characterized by higher expression level of mitochondrial genes (PT-Mito) and consisting of 3.1–5.8% of kidney cortex cells (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The PT-Mito cluster was in proximity to proximal tubule-segment1 (PT-S1) and proximal tubule-segment2 (PT-S2) based on UMAP.
source: Based on UMAP, this PT-Mito cluster was in proximity to proximal tubule-segment1 (PT-S1) and proximal tubule-segment2 (PT-S2) (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by UMAP visualization shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In situ hybridization of mt-Co1 and mt-Atp6 confirmed the presence of transcripts inside some nuclei in many putative PT-Mito segments with high expression of these genes.
source: To confirm the presence of cells giving rise to this cluster, in situ hybridization (ISH) of mt-Co1 and mt-Atp6 were performed. We observed transcripts inside some nuclei in many putative PT-Mito segments with high expression of these genes (Figure 4B and C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ISH data shown in Figure 4B and C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: A similar PT-Mito cluster exists in published human kidney single-nuclear RNA-seq data.
source: We also confirmed the existence of similar PT-Mito cluster in published human kidney single-nuclear RNA-seq data (Wilson et al., 2019) by the re-analysis of the original data (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by re-analysis of published data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: The PT-Mito cluster was observed in both WT and Tg26 kidney in similar ratios.
source: As the PT-Mito cluster was observed in both WT and Tg26 kidney in similar ratios, this new cluster could be a conserved tubular cell cluster, likely not previously reported due to mitochondrial gene filtering criteria implemented in single-nucleus RNA-seq analytic pipelines.
evidence: This is an observation from the data analysis.

claim: The PT-Mito cluster could be a conserved tubular cell cluster, likely not previously reported due to mitochondrial gene filtering criteria implemented in single-nucleus RNA-seq analytic pipelines.
source: As the PT-Mito cluster was observed in both WT and Tg26 kidney in similar ratios, this new cluster could be a conserved tubular cell cluster, likely not previously reported due to mitochondrial gene filtering criteria implemented in single-nucleus RNA-seq analytic pipelines.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observation and knowledge of typical filtering practices.

claim: Pathway analysis of snRNA-seq data showed that oxidative phosphorylation genes were downregulated in the PT-Mito cluster in Tg26 mice, compared to WT mice, with a Z-score of –4.123.
source: Pathway analysis of snRNA-seq data showed that oxidative phosphorylation genes were downregulated in this PT-Mito cluster in Tg26 mice, compared to WT mice, with a Z-score of –4.123.

claim: Oxidative phosphorylation genes were also downregulated in many other cell types in Tg26 mice.

claim: Mitochondrial dysfunction represents a prominent mechanistic pathway that was dysregulated in majority of cell clusters in Tg26 mice.

claim: Mitochondrial dysfunction was pronounced in the PT-Mito cluster in Tg26 mice.

claim: The gene expression profile of the PT-Inj cluster was comparable to profiles previously reported in mouse models of acute kidney injury.

claim: The gene expression profile of the PT-Inj cluster was comparable to profiles previously reported in mouse models of kidney fibrosis.

claim: There is some overlap in molecular pathways between the Tg26 model and the ischemia-reperfusion injury model.

claim: The higher expression of injury marker genes in Tg26 mice was ameliorated with C16 treatment.

evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3B.

claim: There is some overlap of pathological molecular pathways between HIV-associated tubular injury and ischemic injury, especially at later stages when fibrosis appears.
source: This finding suggested some overlap of pathological molecular pathways between HIV-associated tubular injury and ischemic injury, especially at later stages when fibrosis appears.
